evidence.claim: Thomas Jefferson Parkway climbs Carters Mountain just south of Charlottesville, winding toward a summit between Monticello and Montalto.
evidence.quote: The state highway heads east and begins to ascend Carters Mountain, which is part of the Southwest Mountains.  Just west of Michie Tavern, SR 53 winds as it continues to its summit between Monticello to the east and Montalto

evidence.claim: The road continues through curves on its descent to Simeon, then crosses Buck Island Creek near the Rivanna River before entering Fluvanna County.
evidence.quote: SR 53 has a few more curves as it descends the mountain to the hamlet of Simeon

evidence.claim: It is numbered SR 53 and provides access to Thomas Jefferson’s Monticello.
evidence.quote: Known as Thomas Jefferson Parkway

evidence.claim: The parkway’s state-highway history began with a small section from SR 20 toward Monticello, added to the system as SR 714 in 1930.
evidence.quote: A small piece of SR 53, from the west end at SR 20 towards Monticello, was added to the state highway system in 1930 (along with SR 20 north to Charlottesville) as State Route 714

evidence.claim: That section became SR 239 in 1933 and was absorbed into SR 20 in 1941.
evidence.quote: it became State Route 239 in the 1933 renumbering. In 1941, State Route 20 was extended north from Scottsville to Charlottesville via Blenheim and Overton, absorbing SR 239.

evidence.claim: When SR 20 shifted west in 1947, a short piece of its old route became part of SR 53.
evidence.quote: SR 20 was shifted west to its current alignment in 1947; at the same time, current SR 53 was upgraded from State Route 642, and a short piece of old SR 20 became SR 53.

evidence.claim: Start the parkway’s eastward climb at SR 20, pass Michie Tavern and reach the Monticello access road, which crosses above the highway.
evidence.quote: A two-way ramp connects SR 53 with the Monticello access road, which passes over the state highway.

evidence.claim: Descending to Simeon brings the junction with James Monroe Parkway, the road south to Monroe’s estate.
evidence.quote: SR 795 leads south to the estate of James Monroe, Ashlawn-Highland.

evidence.claim: SR 53 continues past the western edge of Lake Monticello to its end at U.S. 15 in Palmyra.
evidence.quote: The state highway passes along the western edge of the suburban resort community of Lake Monticello

evidence.claim: The lane contained workshops and quarters for people Thomas Jefferson enslaved.
